source_papers_profile.paper_title: Drought-induced stress on rainfed and irrigated agriculture: Insights from multi-source satellite-derived ecological indicators
source_papers_profile.paper_type_rationale: The paper explicitly traces causal pathways from climate forcing (precipitation and temperature) to drought state (SPEI3) and then to ecological outcomes (LAI, GPP, GOSIF), while testing irrigation's buffering role. Its core contribution is explanatory mechanism analysis rather than policy design.

source_papers_profile.paper_title: Drought in India: Its impact and mitigation strategies – A review
source_papers_profile.paper_type_rationale: The paper aggregates prior evidence, definitions, and policy/practice recommendations instead of presenting a new single empirical causal model.

source_papers_profile.paper_title: Exploring the Association between Changing Crop Types and Water Scarcity: A Case Study over West-Central India
source_papers_profile.paper_type_rationale: The paper explicitly tests linked climate-agriculture-groundwater pathways and concludes a causal amplification mechanism where crop-type shifts and water management drive drought severity beyond rainfall variability.

source_papers_profile.paper_title: Drought stress effect, tolerance, and management in wheat – a review
source_papers_profile.paper_type_rationale: The article compiles and interprets prior literature on mechanisms and interventions rather than presenting one original causal dataset or a single field experiment.

source_papers_profile.paper_title: Groundwater depletion in India: the influence of seasonal precipitation and land use land cover
source_papers_profile.paper_type_rationale: The paper quantifies directional links from seasonal precipitation and LULCC to groundwater storage variability using trend and correlation evidence across regions and seasons. Its contribution is causal-mechanism oriented rather than policy-design or purely descriptive review.

source_papers_profile.paper_title: Solving groundwater depletion in India while achieving food security
source_papers_profile.paper_type_rationale: The paper explicitly models causal pathways from policy incentives and crop allocation to irrigation demand, groundwater stress, energy use, and farm income via constrained optimization. It is a mechanism study with quantified directional effects, not only policy commentary.

source_papers_profile.paper_title: Combatting groundwater depletion in North-Western India: Obstacles, consequences, and water-saving agronomic approaches
source_papers_profile.paper_type_rationale: The paper synthesizes findings from existing studies and government reports rather than producing new causal estimates from a single empirical dataset. Its contribution is comparative evidence integration across interventions, outcomes, and policy contexts.

source_papers_profile.paper_title: Agricultural Resource Depletion and Arising Concerns of Environmental Ethics in Punjab: A Dire Need of Rescue, Revival and Sustainable Development
source_papers_profile.paper_type_rationale: The article compiles published government statistics and prior studies to narrate resource-depletion patterns and policy implications rather than estimating new causal parameters from primary field data.

source_papers_profile.paper_title: Analyzing the Challenges and Solutions of Sustainable Groundwater Management using Micro-irrigation
source_papers_profile.paper_type_rationale: The article compiles and narrates findings across many prior studies and reports rather than presenting new primary measurements or causal identification from a single dataset.

source_papers_profile.paper_title: Challenges and interventions in water resource management for horticultural crop production in rural and tribal communities in India
source_papers_profile.paper_type_rationale: Single tribal village deep dive with triangulated qualitative evidence and site-specific CropWat/soil data rather than broad statistical causal identification.

source_papers_profile.paper_title: Irrigation in India: Status and challenges
source_papers_profile.paper_type_rationale: The manuscript is explicitly framed as a status-and-challenges viewpoint that synthesizes prior studies, national programme descriptions, and secondary statistics rather than presenting new identified causal estimates at fine spatial resolution.

source_papers_profile.paper_title: Risks in rainfed agriculture and adaptation strategies in India: Profile and socio-economic correlates
source_papers_profile.paper_type_rationale: Empirical case study using primary survey data and beta regression of an adaptation index on socio-economic covariates in two cotton districts of Maharashtra; it descriptively profiles risks and statistically tests covariates rather than building a fully specified end-to-end mechanism model.

source_papers_profile.paper_title: Livelihood vulnerability of food systems in Agro-Ecological Region I of Southern Zambia
source_papers_profile.paper_type_rationale: The paper quantifies exposure, sensitivity and adaptive capacity and tests how these components propagate into LVI-IPCC vulnerability and food-security outcomes; it also uses regression and validation analyses, so it is a mechanism-oriented empirical study rather than a purely descriptive case study.

source_papers_profile.paper_title: Dry and Rainfed Agriculture- Characteristics and Issues to Enhance the Prosperity of Indian Farming Community
source_papers_profile.paper_type_rationale: The paper synthesises and integrates prior literature on dry/rainfed agriculture characteristics and soil-water conservation strategies; it does not present new primary data, statistical models, or original empirical analysis - meeting the definition of a review.

unified_mechanism_blocks.description: Merged primary cross-stressor pathways observed across drought, groundwater stress, irrigation challenges, and rainfed risk papers.

primary_edges.mechanism: Excess irrigation demand met by sustained groundwater pumping draws aquifer storage faster than recharge; integrated over decades this produces a strong negative trend in water-table depth.
primary_edges.conditions: Narrative national synthesis; spatial heterogeneity emphasized elsewhere in the paper
primary_edges.from_var_value_range_merged: Water-intensive crops expanded in drought years including 2002, 2012, 2014, 2015.; Current irrigation 146 Billion m3; under redesigned allocation 130 Billion m3 (capped).; Punjab irrigation savings 38 or 34 billion m3 under zero/capped scenarios relative to current.; Extraction stages >100% in Punjab, Rajasthan, Haryana (2022).; Water demand increased twofold then manifold (narrative); tubewells increased from 192,000 (1970-71) to 1,276,200 (2008-09); 91% national water use for livestock and irrigation; extraction 239.16 BCM vs extractable 398.08 BCM (cited); High seasonal irrigation demand (311.4 mm net need class); Excess demand met through over-exploitation of groundwater
primary_edges.to_var_value_range_merged: Groundwater fell by about 4-5 m over most districts in period.; Observed depletion around 1-3 m/year in stressed states.; Objective includes reversing around 1-2 m/year depletion in Punjab.; About 4.0 +/- 1.0 cm/year decline (2000-2008) in NW states in cited analysis.; 0.94 m/year average water-table decline since 2004-07; Depletion narrative: extraction exceeds recharge in many settings (review); Falling well levels and dam drawdown (observed); 1-2 m/year decline in water table (quoted national observation); 77% of farmers report unreliable groundwater supply (proxy for declining tables); Ground-water levels deepened almost double since 1973

primary_edges.mechanism: Cheap electricity subsidies lower marginal pumping costs, expanding tubewell irrigation capacity and water applied per hectare.
primary_edges.conditions: PDS-favored irrigation regions with high groundwater dependence.
primary_edges.from_var_value_range_merged: Punjab subsidy outlay example INR 65 billion.; Haryana subsidy burden includes about $158.26/ha for surplus irrigation and about $0.11 billion state subsidy for extra irrigation.
primary_edges.to_var_value_range_merged: Current national irrigation around 146 Billion m3.; Extraction stage in 2022: Punjab 165.99%, Rajasthan 151.07%, Haryana 134.14%.

primary_edges.mechanism: Annual rainfall is the primary supply term in the soil-water balance; under <750 mm dryland conditions with ill-distributed monsoon, soil moisture cannot be replenished above PWP for sustained crop growth.
primary_edges.conditions: Dryland (<750 mm) and rainfed tracts of Punjab, Haryana, Rajasthan, MP, Maharashtra, AP, Karnataka
primary_edges.from_var_value_range_merged: Extreme drought examples include very low seasonal rainfall values; Decline in precipitation of 16.09 mm annually cited.; Dryland <750 mm; Rainfed >750 mm; SW monsoon ~75% of dry-land rainfall
primary_edges.to_var_value_range_merged: Soil moisture below 15 bar (PWP) results in failure of crops in dryland agriculture

primary_edges.mechanism: High fixed costs per hectare and limited collateral on tiny holdings slow investment in emitters, filters, and pressurized networks.
primary_edges.from_var_value_range_merged: 89.4% holdings classified small-scale in cited statistic; Plot sizes 0.16–0.60 ha dominant
primary_edges.to_var_value_range_merged: MI penetration 9% NSA despite growth from 5.5%; Drip/sprinkler not adopted (stated incompatibility with small plots/cost)

primary_edges.mechanism: Contour bunds, check dams, terraces, and in-situ / ex-situ moisture harvesting slow runoff and increase infiltration, raising the net recharge rate to shallow aquifers in rainfed watersheds.
primary_edges.conditions: Adequate structure density and maintenance in watershed/urban systems.
primary_edges.from_var_value_range_merged: Water harvesting contribution about 38.53% of total recharge in cited micro-shed case.
primary_edges.to_var_value_range_merged: Natural recharge estimated 11-16% of annual rainfall in cited context.

primary_edges.mechanism: Persistent soil moisture below the permanent wilting point precludes water uptake by roots, causing partial or complete crop failure in dryland agriculture.
primary_edges.conditions: Dryland with shallow soils and limited moisture buffer
primary_edges.to_var_value_range_merged: 2002-03 decline 38.66 million tonnes; kharif production decline about 5-7%; Drylands account for 80% of coarse cereals, 50% of maize, 65% of chickpea/pigeonpea, 81% of groundnut, 88% of soybean, and ~50% of cotton output - but at extremely low productivity per ha

primary_edges.mechanism: Efficiency and better water management can maintain or raise yield while reducing applied water, though outcomes vary by practice and site.
primary_edges.conditions: Technology match to local soils/climate and proper agronomic management.
primary_edges.from_var_value_range_merged: 10% WUE improvement; SRI reported about 23% water saving and up to 46% productivity increase in cited setting.
primary_edges.to_var_value_range_merged: Potential additional output about 50 million tonnes foodgrains; DSR often shows initial 2-6% grain-yield reduction in some contexts; LLL increased crop yields (rice/wheat/sugarcane) in cited cases.

primary_edges.mechanism: Green Revolution packages tied HYV seeds to intensive irrigation, raising long-run irrigation duty in favorable agroecologies.
primary_edges.from_var_value_range_merged: 190% cropping intensity (highest India); narrative cites >200%; Intensive irrigation named with HYV adoption
primary_edges.to_var_value_range_merged: Excessive groundwater extraction named outcome pathway

primary_edges.mechanism: Within-season dry spells defined as <15 mm rainfall in consecutive weeks deplete root-zone soil moisture even when seasonal totals are adequate, producing moisture stress at critical phenological stages.
primary_edges.conditions: Kharif crop growth window in dry/rainfed tracts
primary_edges.from_var_value_range_merged: Dry spell threshold: <15 mm rainfall in consecutive weeks
primary_edges.to_var_value_range_merged: Soil moisture below 15-bar PWP under prolonged dry spells

primary_edges.mechanism: When potential evapotranspiration exceeds rainfall supply, soil moisture is drawn down faster than it is replenished; under dry-tract regimes the rainfall-PET balance is negative for much of the year.
primary_edges.conditions: Periods when PET exceeds rainfall in dry/rainfed tracts
primary_edges.to_var_value_range_merged: Soil moisture below 15-bar PWP causes crop failure

primary_edges.mechanism: Groundwater decline reduces irrigation reliability and available crop water, contributing to lower staple crop yields.
primary_edges.from_var_value_range_merged: National seasonal decline magnitude includes -6.52 mm/year in summer.; 0.94 m/year average decline since 2004-07

primary_edges.mechanism: Lower mean rainfall in the south-western belt increases reliance on irrigation to sustain rice-wheat and cotton systems.
primary_edges.from_var_value_range_merged: ~360 mm/year average rainfall (Zone C); Oct–Dec very low rain; Jan–May dry; annual mean 2131 mm concentrated in monsoon
primary_edges.to_var_value_range_merged: Supplemental then full irrigation required (CropWat seasonal totals)

secondary_edges.mechanism: High fertilizer prices and shortages of urea / phosphatic fertilizers force sub-optimal application or skipping of doses; ex-post farmers also reduce fertilizer applications under low-rainfall years, suppressing yields.
secondary_edges.from_var_value_range_merged: 239-251 kg/ha total fertilizer intensity (cited ranges); Ex-post: 21% of farmers reduce fertilizer application; ~89% report high fertilizer price; Rainfed regions consume hardly 25% of total fertilizer consumption of India
secondary_edges.to_var_value_range_merged: Drylands: 80% of coarse cereals output but very low yield per ha

secondary_edges.mechanism: Higher near-surface temperature raises the saturation vapour deficit and energy available for evaporation, increasing potential evapotranspiration in the dry tracts.
secondary_edges.conditions: Late April-early May summer peak in dry tracts
secondary_edges.from_var_value_range_merged: Temperature increase rate about 0.06 C annually.; 95.4% increasing maximum temperatures; 55.1% increasing minimum temperatures; average temperature 21 deg C; Maximum temperature > 41 deg C in late April-early May; minimum 14-15 deg C
secondary_edges.to_var_value_range_merged: Wheat water requirement 300-500 mm.; High evapotranspiration rates reported; no numeric ET value

secondary_edges.mechanism: Higher application efficiency lowers gross irrigation requirement per unit evapotranspiration when schedules match crop demand.
secondary_edges.conditions: Rebound effects controlled and adoption paired with governance constraints.
secondary_edges.from_var_value_range_merged: AWD reduced irrigation water 26-52%; LLL saved about 21% irrigation in one cited study.; PRD and drip trials showing reduced seasonal water applications (cited ranges in meta-regression); System efficiency 0.7 (furrow)
secondary_edges.to_var_value_range_merged: Micro-irrigation savings partly offset (about half) by expanded irrigated area in cited evidence.; Fan et al. wheat: 31.4% irrigation reduction tied to 14.8% grain loss scenario; cotton 51.4% water reduction; Applied ~252 m³/season vs modeled gross 213.46 m³

secondary_edges.mechanism: Reallocating crop area away from water-intensive rice in arid procurement states reduces aggregate irrigation requirement.
secondary_edges.conditions: Optimized procurement/cropping pattern under production and nutrition constraints.
secondary_edges.from_var_value_range_merged: Increase in high-water crop production and area after around 2000.; Rice area reduced >75% in key northwestern sourcing regions.; Rice procurement linked to at least 50% of observed groundwater decline over 34 years in cited evidence.
secondary_edges.to_var_value_range_merged: Augmented water supply demand reported with increasing cash-crop yield.; 146 Billion m3 current vs 130 Billion m3 Irrigation Capped and 0 in Irrigation Zero.; India extraction 239.16 bcm in 2022.

secondary_edges.mechanism: Falling water tables force farmers to deepen existing wells or drill new bore-wells to chase the receding aquifer, raising operational well depth.
secondary_edges.from_var_value_range_merged: Deepening of water tables reported during drought years; Ground-water levels deepened almost double since 1973
secondary_edges.to_var_value_range_merged: 25% of farmers ex-post adopt 'digging/deepening well'; 57% report failure of bore wells; Centrifuge pumps no longer effective in IGP - replaced by submersibles

secondary_edges.mechanism: Drip and sprinkler systems target root zones and timing, cutting evaporative and distribution losses versus flood methods.
secondary_edges.from_var_value_range_merged: Penetration 9% NSA (2020) context; qualitative mechanism plus case WUE gains; Drip/sprinkler not adopted (qualitative)
secondary_edges.to_var_value_range_merged: PRD +60% WUE; meta-regression and trials cited for efficiency gains; Furrow system efficiency ~70%

secondary_edges.mechanism: Without storage, monsoon water is not retained for dry-season horticulture, forcing higher supplemental irrigation withdrawals.
secondary_edges.conditions: Tribal village with hilly runoff; ~90% rainfall loss narrative
secondary_edges.from_var_value_range_merged: Almost 90% of annual rainfall not captured by harvesting/storage (cited)
secondary_edges.to_var_value_range_merged: Seasonal irrigation requirement 311.4 mm vs 89.4 mm effective rain (bitter gourd)

secondary_edges.mechanism: Progressive groundwater depletion alters hydrogeochemical conditions such that aquifers can become saline and land subsidence is asserted as a linked risk in the review narrative.
secondary_edges.conditions: Review-level causal language; not quantified for Indian districts in this paper

secondary_edges.mechanism: Lower precipitation decreases climatic water balance and drives SPEI3 toward drought values.
secondary_edges.from_var_value_range_merged: 2012 precipitation decreased by 13.15%; June-September cumulative reduction about 51.50 mm; Drought framing uses rainfall deficit >25%; severe >50%; agricultural drought below 50-75% monsoon normal
secondary_edges.to_var_value_range_merged: SPEI3 drought onset threshold < -0.5; MI = (P-PET)/PET x 100

secondary_edges.mechanism: Deficient or untimely monsoon rainfall is the proximate trigger of drought events at block level in the rainfed cotton belt of Maharashtra.
secondary_edges.conditions: Rainfed kharif cotton in Vidarbha / Khandesh agro-climatic zones
secondary_edges.from_var_value_range_merged: Overall whole-monsoon trend -0.111 mm/year; district-level mixed trends.; Late onset of monsoon flagged by 90.9% of farmers; untimely rainfall by 81.7%
secondary_edges.to_var_value_range_merged: Severe drought years identified: 1982, 1987, 2002, 2009, 2012, 2014, 2015.; Drought cited as top weather risk by 91.3% of farmers

secondary_edges.mechanism: Higher net recharge replenishes the aquifer, slowing or reversing the negative trend in groundwater level; conservation interventions that lift recharge therefore close the loop on the groundwater-overexploitation mechanism in the IGP.
secondary_edges.conditions: Watershed-treated rainfed catchments and IGP zones where structures, residue retention and tillage interventions are operational
secondary_edges.from_var_value_range_merged: Negative balances: Punjab -11.05 bcm, Rajasthan -4.39 bcm, Haryana -2.08 bcm.
secondary_edges.to_var_value_range_merged: Overexploited blocks in 2022: Punjab about 76%, Rajasthan about 72%, Haryana about 61%, Delhi about 44%.; Ground-water levels deepened almost double since 1973 in the absence of effective recharge management

secondary_edges.mechanism: Adaptive capacity offsets exposure in the LVI-IPCC formula; lower adaptive capacity widens the exposure-capacity gap and increases vulnerability.
secondary_edges.from_var_value_range_merged: Adaptive capacity district values 0.4911-0.5092; household mean 0.50
